question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The scientific study of the structure and form of animals and plants
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Morphology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Morphology" is the scientific study of the structure and form of animals and plants (from Greek 'morphe' = form + 'logos' = study). (आकृति विज्ञान)

◦ Example: In morphology, we study the shape, size and structure of organisms and their parts.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Zoology" is the study of animals only.

• Option 3 "Biology" is the general study of living organisms.

• Option 4 "Botany" is the study of plants only.

• None of these specifically means the study of "structure and form", which is what "morphology" denotes.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: Anatomy (study of internal structure of the body), Physiology (study of functions of living organisms), Ecology (study of organisms and their environment), Etymology (study of the origin of words).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Machenical.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Machenical" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Mechanical", meaning relating to machines or operated by machinery. (यांत्रिक)

◦ Example: The factory suffered a mechanical failure.

• Spelling key: ME + CHA + NI + CAL (from "mechanic" + "-al").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Annual" (happening once a year), "Technical" (relating to a particular subject/skill) and "Regulator" (a person or device that regulates) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Word family: machine (मशीन), mechanic (मिस्त्री), mechanism (तंत्र), mechanical (यांत्रिक), mechanically (adverb). Note that "machine" has "a" but "mechanical" has "e" after the "m".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She ______ the book to her friend.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. lent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "lend" means to give something to someone for a short time, expecting it back. Its past tense/past participle is "lent" (lend – lent – lent). The sentence describes a completed past action, so "lent" fits. (उधार देना)

◦ Correct: She lent the book to her friend.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "laned" is not a word.

• Option 2 "leant" is the past form of "lean" (to bend/incline), not "lend".

• Option 3 "lend" is the base form; the sentence needs the past tense.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "lend" (to give on loan — the giver lends) with "borrow" (to take on loan — the taker borrows): "She lent me a pen" = "I borrowed a pen from her".

question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error.

The beutiful flowers bloomed in the garden.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. beautiful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "beautiful", meaning pleasing to the senses; very attractive. (सुंदर)

◦ Correct: The beautiful flowers bloomed in the garden.

• Spelling key: BEAU + TI + FUL — "beauty" changes its "y" to "i" and adds the suffix "-ful" (with a single "l").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "beautifull" wrongly doubles the final "l".

• Option 2 "beiutiful" and Option 4 "beautifuul" have wrong letter sequences.

NOTE

• The suffix "-ful" always has one "l": beautiful, wonderful, careful, helpful, successful. The adverb doubles it: beautiful → beautifully.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

We talked over the matter for two hours; unfortunately, we could not reach a decision.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Discussed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "talk over" means to discuss a matter thoroughly, especially to reach a decision. (किसी विषय पर विस्तार से चर्चा करना)

◦ Correct meaning: We discussed the matter for two hours but could not reach a decision.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Argued" and Option 2 "Quarrelled" suggest disagreement or conflict, which "talk over" does not imply.

• Option 3 "Debated" means a formal argument with two opposing sides — again not the neutral sense of "talk over".

NOTE

• Useful phrasal verbs with "talk": talk over (discuss), talk into (persuade to do), talk out of (persuade not to do), talk down to (speak condescendingly), talk back (reply rudely).

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
option_1: The Nile is the longest river in the world with a length about approximately 6650 km.
option_2: The Nile is the long river in the world with a length about approximately 6650 km.
option_3: The Nile is the most long river in the world of a length of approximately 6650 km.
option_4: The Nile is the longest river in the world with a length of approximately 6650 km.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The Nile is the longest river in the world with a length of approximately 6650 km.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A comparison with the whole world ("in the world") requires the superlative degree — "the longest".

• The correct noun phrase is "a length of approximately 6650 km" — the noun "length" takes the preposition "of" before the measurement.

◦ Correct: The Nile is the longest river in the world with a length of approximately 6650 km.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 uses the wrong preposition phrase "about approximately" (redundant and unidiomatic).

• Option 2 uses the positive degree "long" where the superlative is needed.

• Option 3 "the most long" is wrong — short adjectives form the superlative with "-est" (long → longest), not with "most".

NOTE

• Superlative pattern: the + adjective-est/most + noun + in/of + group ("the longest river in the world"). GK bonus: the Nile (Africa, about 6,650 km) is traditionally regarded as the longest river in the world; the Amazon carries the largest volume of water.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Like a dying duck in a thunderstorm
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Dejected or hopeless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "like a dying duck in a thunderstorm" means having a dejected, hopeless or helpless look; utterly forlorn. (निराश और हताश दिखना)

◦ Example: After failing the exam, he sat in the corner like a dying duck in a thunderstorm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• The idiom paints the picture of a helpless duck caught in a storm — hence a look of misery and despair.

• Options 1, 3 and 4 are literal or unrelated interpretations; idioms must never be taken literally.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "down in the dumps" (sad/depressed), "a lame duck" (a helpless/ineffective person), "take to something like a duck to water" (learn something very naturally), "a sitting duck" (an easy target).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Amit, the stand-up comedian, delivered a hilarious performance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. serious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hilarious" means extremely funny; causing great amusement. Its antonym is "serious" — grave, solemn, not funny. (बेहद हास्यप्रद का विलोम — गंभीर)

◦ With the antonym: Amit, the stand-up comedian, delivered a serious performance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "spleen" (an abdominal organ; also bad temper), Option 2 "ideological" (relating to ideas/beliefs) and Option 4 "pertinent" (relevant) are unrelated to the funny–serious contrast.

NOTE

• Synonyms of hilarious: uproarious, comical, side-splitting, amusing. Antonyms: serious, grave, solemn, sombre.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options..
option_1: A lot of books and notes place in order look most fascinating.
option_2: A lot of books and notes placed in order look fascinating.
option_3: A lot of books and notes placed on order looks most fascinating.
option_4: A lot of book and notes placed in order looks most fascinating.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A lot of books and notes placed in order look fascinating.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The past participle "placed" is needed to describe the books and notes ("books and notes placed in order" = books and notes that have been placed in order).

• The correct phrase is "in order" (arranged properly), not "on order".

• The plural subject "books and notes" takes the plural verb "look", not "looks".

◦ Correct: A lot of books and notes placed in order look fascinating.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly uses the base form "place" instead of the participle "placed", and "most fascinating" is unnecessary without any comparison.

• Option 3 has the wrong preposition ("on order") and a wrong singular verb "looks".

• Option 4 uses the singular "book" after "a lot of" (which needs a plural/uncountable noun) and the wrong verb "looks".

NOTE

• "A lot of + plural noun" takes a plural verb: "A lot of books are on the shelf." A participle phrase ("placed in order") does not change the number of the subject.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The train is running / late by six hours / so it / cannot make over the time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. cannot make over the time.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb for compensating for lost time is "make up", not "make over". So the segment should be "cannot make up the time" (i.e., cannot compensate for the delay). (खोए समय की भरपाई करना)

◦ Correct: The train is running late by six hours, so it cannot make up the time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "The train is running", "late by six hours" and "so it" are all grammatically correct.

• "Make over" means to transfer ownership or to transform someone's appearance — it does not fit here.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "make": make up (compensate/invent/reconcile), make up for (compensate for), make out (understand/discern), make off (run away), make over (transfer/transform).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The writer's __________ prose resonated with readers, evoking powerful emotions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. eloquent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Eloquent" means fluent, expressive and persuasive in writing or speech. Prose that "resonated with readers, evoking powerful emotions" must be expressive — hence "eloquent". (प्रभावशाली / वाक्पटु)

◦ Correct: The writer's eloquent prose resonated with readers, evoking powerful emotions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "banal" (boring, unoriginal) and Option 3 "mundane" (dull, ordinary) contradict the idea of evoking powerful emotions.

• Option 2 "sporadic" (occurring irregularly/occasionally) does not describe the quality of prose.

NOTE

• Synonyms of eloquent: articulate, expressive, fluent, persuasive, silver-tongued. Antonyms: inarticulate, dull, banal.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The teacher emphasised the importance of ___________ correct grammar and punctuation in our writing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. using.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After a preposition ("of"), a verb must take the gerund (-ing) form. So "the importance of using correct grammar" is correct. (पूर्वसर्ग के बाद gerund)

◦ Correct: The teacher emphasised the importance of using correct grammar and punctuation in our writing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "used" (past tense/participle), 2 "uses" (third-person singular) and 4 "use" (base form) cannot follow the preposition "of" as verb forms.

NOTE

• Rule: Preposition + V-ing (gerund) — "fond of reading", "interested in learning", "importance of using", "tired of waiting". A gerund works as a noun.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Gold is much costly than any other metal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. more.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree. The comparative of "costly" here is formed with "more" — "more costly than any other metal". (तुलनात्मक डिग्री)

◦ Correct: Gold is more costly than any other metal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "most" is the superlative and cannot be used with "than".

• Option 2 "most costlier" combines a superlative with a comparative — always wrong (double degree).

• Option 3 "many" is a quantifier for countable nouns, not a degree word.

NOTE

• Pattern for comparing one thing with all others of its class: comparative + than + any other + singular noun ("Gold is more costly/costlier than any other metal"). Never mix "more" with "-er" (no "more costlier").

question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

The orator declared that the women are ___________ than the men.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. more intelligent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" demands the comparative degree. "Intelligent" is a long adjective (three syllables), so its comparative is formed with "more" — "more intelligent". (अधिक बुद्धिमान)

◦ Correct: The orator declared that the women are more intelligent than the men.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "most intelligent" is the superlative — it cannot be followed by "than".

• Option 2 "intelligenter" is not a word; long adjectives never take "-er".

• Option 4 "intelligent" (positive degree) cannot be used with "than".

NOTE

• Adjectives of three or more syllables form degrees with more/most: intelligent – more intelligent – most intelligent; beautiful – more beautiful – most beautiful.

question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

Jack always looks handsome, even if he is a __________ out of style.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. little.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiomatic expression "a little" means slightly / to a small degree. "Even if he is a little out of style" = even if he is slightly unfashionable. (थोड़ा-सा)

◦ Correct: Jack always looks handsome, even if he is a little out of style.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "more little" is ungrammatical (the comparative of "little" is "less/smaller", never "more little").

• Options 3 "less" and 4 "least" cannot follow the article "a" in this construction ("a less/least out of style" is meaningless).

NOTE

• "A little" (positive sense — some amount) is used with uncountable ideas/degrees: "a little tired", "a little out of style". Compare "little" without "a" (almost none): "There is little hope."

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

High-altitude climbing poses significant risks due to factors like altitude sickness, hypothermia and extreme weather conditions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. inconsequential.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Significant" means important; considerable; noteworthy. Its antonym is "inconsequential" — unimportant, trivial, of no consequence. (महत्त्वपूर्ण का विलोम — महत्त्वहीन/तुच्छ)

◦ With the antonym: High-altitude climbing poses inconsequential risks ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "magnificent" (very impressive/grand), Option 3 "plentiful" (existing in large amounts) and Option 4 "tempestuous" (stormy/turbulent) are not opposites of "significant".

NOTE

• Synonyms of significant: important, considerable, substantial, notable. Antonyms: insignificant, inconsequential, trivial, negligible, minor.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined segment in the given sentence.

It's important to bring up sensitive topics in a respectful manner.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Strong.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Respectful" means showing politeness, courtesy and regard for others. Among the given options, "strong" (in the sense of harsh, forceful, blunt) works as its antonym — a "strong manner" is the opposite of a gentle, respectful manner. (सम्मानजनक का विलोम — कठोर/तेज़)

◦ With the antonym: ... to bring up sensitive topics in a strong (harsh) manner.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Cordial" (warm and friendly) and Option 4 "Considerate" (careful not to hurt others) are synonyms of respectful, so they cannot be the antonym.

• Option 2 "Drowsy" (sleepy) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of respectful: polite, courteous, considerate, cordial, deferential. Antonyms: disrespectful, rude, harsh, impolite.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The croissant was _________, as was the coffee.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. excellent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Excellent" means extremely good; of very high quality — the natural adjective for describing food and drink. (उत्कृष्ट / बहुत बढ़िया)

◦ Correct: The croissant was excellent, as was the coffee.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "eloquent" (expressive in speech/writing) and Option 3 "ambitious" (having strong desire for success) describe people, not food.

• Option 4 "inferior" (of poor quality) gives a negative sense, but the structure "as was the coffee" suggests praise being extended to both items; "excellent" is the most natural choice.

NOTE

• "As was the coffee" is an inverted comparative structure meaning "and the coffee was too". Synonyms of excellent: superb, outstanding, first-rate, exceptional.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Idle
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Unoccupied.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Idle" means not working; not active; doing nothing. Its closest synonym is "unoccupied" — not busy, without work. (बेकार / निठल्ला)

◦ Example: The workers remained idle/unoccupied because the machines had broken down.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Unsafe" (dangerous), Option 3 "Ungrateful" (not thankful) and Option 4 "Uneasy" (anxious/uncomfortable) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of idle: inactive, unoccupied, unemployed, lazy, indolent. Antonyms: busy, active, occupied, industrious. Do not confuse "idle" (निठल्ला) with "idol" (मूर्ति) — they are homophones.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Doves _________ in the sky above me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. soar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Soar" (verb) means to fly high in the air. Birds like doves "soar in the sky". (ऊँचा उड़ना)

◦ Correct: Doves soar in the sky above me.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "sore" (adjective — painful; e.g., a sore throat) is a homophone of "soar" but has a different meaning.

• Option 2 "shore" (the land along the edge of a sea/lake) and Option 3 "sour" (having an acidic taste) do not fit.

NOTE

• Common homophone pairs asked in SSC exams: soar/sore, flour/flower, bare/bear, principal/principle, stationary/stationery, weather/whether. "Soar" is also used figuratively: "Prices soared" (rose sharply).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It is true that strangers meeting for the first time seem to feel ____1____ if they do not engage _____ 2_____ small talk. Usually, this is ______3______ and even necessary if strangers are to size each other up. But, this small talk aside, what are some _____4______ rules for general conversation? In the first place, certain _____5_____ should be taboo. Kitchen topics, bus time-tables and other dull or specialised things should be barred from general discussion.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. uncomfortable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an adjective after "feel" to describe the strangers' state. "Uncomfortable" (uneasy, awkward) fits perfectly — strangers feel uncomfortable if they do not engage in small talk. (असहज)

◦ Correct: ... strangers meeting for the first time seem to feel uncomfortable if they do not engage in small talk.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "discomforts" and Option 4 "comforts" are nouns, which cannot follow the linking verb "feel" here.

• Option 2 "comforting" gives the opposite (positive) sense — silence among strangers is awkward, not comforting.

NOTE

• Linking verbs (feel, seem, look, appear, become) are followed by adjectives, not adverbs/nouns: "feel uncomfortable", "seem happy", "look tired".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It is true that strangers meeting for the first time seem to feel ____1____ if they do not engage _____ 2_____ small talk. Usually, this is ______3______ and even necessary if strangers are to size each other up. But, this small talk aside, what are some _____4______ rules for general conversation? In the first place, certain _____5_____ should be taboo. Kitchen topics, bus time-tables and other dull or specialised things should be barred from general discussion.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "engage" takes the fixed preposition "in" when it means "to take part in an activity" — "engage in small talk / conversation / an activity". (किसी गतिविधि में भाग लेना)

◦ Correct: ... if they do not engage in small talk.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Engage by", "engage on" and "engage from" are not standard collocations for taking part in an activity.

• "Engage with" (interact with someone/something) and "be engaged to" (betrothed to a person) have different meanings.

NOTE

• Fixed preposition pairs often tested: engage in, indulge in, participate in, succeed in, believe in, deal in (trade) vs deal with (handle).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It is true that strangers meeting for the first time seem to feel ____1____ if they do not engage _____ 2_____ small talk. Usually, this is ______3______ and even necessary if strangers are to size each other up. But, this small talk aside, what are some _____4______ rules for general conversation? In the first place, certain _____5_____ should be taboo. Kitchen topics, bus time-tables and other dull or specialised things should be barred from general discussion.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. harmless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence says small talk is "______ and even necessary if strangers are to size each other up". The adjective "harmless" (causing no harm; innocent) pairs naturally with "necessary" — small talk is harmless and even useful. (हानिरहित)

◦ Correct: Usually, this is harmless and even necessary if strangers are to size each other up.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "happy" does not describe "small talk" idiomatically here.

• Option 2 "comedy" and Option 4 "remedy" are nouns and cannot fill an adjective slot before "and even necessary".

• "To size someone up" means to form a judgement about a person.

NOTE

• Suffix "-less" means "without": harmless (without harm), careless, fearless, useless. Its opposite here would be "harmful".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It is true that strangers meeting for the first time seem to feel ____1____ if they do not engage _____ 2_____ small talk. Usually, this is ______3______ and even necessary if strangers are to size each other up. But, this small talk aside, what are some _____4______ rules for general conversation? In the first place, certain _____5_____ should be taboo. Kitchen topics, bus time-tables and other dull or specialised things should be barred from general discussion.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. elementary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Elementary" means basic; fundamental; relating to the simplest principles. The passage asks about the basic rules of conversation — "what are some elementary rules for general conversation?" (प्रारंभिक / बुनियादी)

◦ Correct: ... what are some elementary rules for general conversation?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "eliminating" (removing) is a participle, not a fitting adjective for "rules".

• Option 2 "alimentary" relates to food/digestion (as in "alimentary canal").

• Option 3 "illuminative" (giving light/insight) does not collocate with "rules for conversation".

NOTE

• Do not confuse the near-sounding words: elementary (basic), alimentary (relating to nourishment), elemental (relating to the forces of nature). Such confusable pairs are frequently tested in SSC exams.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It is true that strangers meeting for the first time seem to feel ____1____ if they do not engage _____ 2_____ small talk. Usually, this is ______3______ and even necessary if strangers are to size each other up. But, this small talk aside, what are some _____4______ rules for general conversation? In the first place, certain _____5_____ should be taboo. Kitchen topics, bus time-tables and other dull or specialised things should be barred from general discussion.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. subjects.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The next sentence gives examples — "Kitchen topics, bus time-tables and other dull or specialised things should be barred from general discussion". So certain "subjects" (topics of conversation) should be taboo. (विषय)

◦ Correct: In the first place, certain subjects should be taboo.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "books", 3 "objects" and 4 "essays" do not match the context of topics of conversation being "barred from general discussion".

• "Taboo" means forbidden or banned by social custom. (वर्जित)

NOTE

• "Subject" and "topic" are synonyms in the sense of "a matter being discussed". The clue-based method — reading the sentence after the blank — is the key strategy for cloze tests in SSC exams.

question: As per the World Happiness Index 2023, which of the following countries secured the highest rank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nepal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the World Happiness Index (Report) 2023, Nepal secured the highest rank (78th) among the given South Asian countries — ahead of Pakistan (108th), Sri Lanka (112th), India (126th) and Bangladesh (118th). (नेपाल — दक्षिण एशिया में सर्वोच्च रैंक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The World Happiness Report is published by the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN), released every year around 20 March (International Day of Happiness).

• Finland topped the 2023 report (for the sixth consecutive year), followed by Denmark and Iceland; Afghanistan was at the bottom.

• The index is based on factors such as GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity and perception of corruption.

NOTE

• India ranked 126th out of 137 countries in the World Happiness Report 2023 — lower than all its given neighbours.

question: Atmospheric temperature usually decreases with altitude, but sometimes this phenomenon gets reversed in the troposphere. This phenomenon is known as _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Temperature Inversion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Normally temperature decreases with altitude in the troposphere (at about 6.5°C per 1,000 m — the normal lapse rate). When this is reversed and temperature increases with height, the phenomenon is called "Temperature Inversion". (तापमान व्युत्क्रमण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ideal conditions for inversion: long winter nights, clear skies, calm and stable air, dry air and snow-covered surfaces — the ground cools rapidly by radiation and chills the air near it.

• Inversion is common in mountain valleys (cold air drains down the slopes at night — "air drainage"), which is why orchards and settlements in hills are located on slopes, not valley floors.

• Inversion traps smoke, dust and pollutants near the ground, causing fog and smog.

NOTE

• The Adiabatic Lapse Rate is the rate of cooling/warming of a rising or sinking air parcel due to pressure change; Global Warming is the long-term rise in Earth's average temperature — both are different phenomena.

question: What is the name of the German Chancellor who visited India in February 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Olaf Scholz.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• German Chancellor Olaf Scholz paid a state visit to India on 25–26 February 2023 — his first visit to India as Chancellor. He held talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on trade, clean energy, defence and skilled-workforce mobility. (ओलाफ शोल्ज़ — जर्मन चांसलर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Olaf Scholz became the Chancellor of Germany in December 2021, succeeding Angela Merkel (Chancellor 2005–2021).

• Germany's capital is Berlin; its currency is the Euro; its Parliament is the Bundestag.

• India and Germany have a Strategic Partnership (since 2000) and hold Inter-Governmental Consultations (IGC).

NOTE

• Willy Brandt was a former West German Chancellor (1969–74), famous for the "Brandt Commission" reports on international development.

question: In the final match of the Asian Games _________ held in Jakarta, Indonesia, India secured gold by defeating South Korea with a score of 2-1 in football.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1962.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the 1962 Asian Games held in Jakarta, Indonesia, the Indian football team won the gold medal by defeating South Korea 2-1 in the final. (1962 एशियाई खेल — जकार्ता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This was India's second Asian Games football gold — the first was at the inaugural 1951 Asian Games in New Delhi.

• The 1962 victory came under coach Syed Abdul Rahim, regarded as the architect of Indian football's "golden era"; stars included Chuni Goswami (captain), P. K. Banerjee and Jarnail Singh.

• The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951; the Games are governed by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).

NOTE

• The 1950s–60s are called the golden era of Indian football — India also finished fourth in the 1956 Melbourne Olympics.

question: As per the Constitution of India, every Governor, before entering upon his office, will make and subscribe an oath in the presence of the ________.
option_4: Chief Justice of the High Court
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chief Justice of the High Court.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Article 159 of the Constitution, every Governor, before entering upon his office, makes and subscribes an oath in the presence of the Chief Justice of the High Court of the state (or, in his absence, the senior-most judge of that High Court available). (अनुच्छेद 159 — उच्च न्यायालय के मुख्य न्यायाधीश के समक्ष शपथ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Governor is appointed by the President (Article 155), must be at least 35 years of age (Article 157) and holds office during the pleasure of the President (Article 156).

• The President's oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India (Article 60); the Chief Minister and state ministers are administered the oath by the Governor.

NOTE

• Governor-related Articles: 153 (Governors of states), 154 (executive power), 155 (appointment), 156 (term), 157–158 (qualifications/conditions), 159 (oath), 161 (pardoning power), 163 (Council of Ministers to aid and advise).

question: The famous novel ‘The house of blue mangoes’ is written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is David Davidar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous novel "The House of Blue Mangoes" (2002) was written by David Davidar, an Indian novelist and publisher (co-founder of the Aleph Book Company and former head of Penguin India). The novel traces three generations of the Dorai family in a South Indian village. (डेविड डेविडर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Romila Thapar is a renowned historian of ancient India (works: "Ashoka and the Decline of the Mauryas", "Early India").

• Shashi Tharoor wrote "The Great Indian Novel", "An Era of Darkness" and "Why I Am a Hindu".

• Anees Salim wrote "The Blind Lady's Descendants" (Sahitya Akademi Award 2018).

NOTE

• Books and authors form a regular part of SSC GK — remember David Davidar's other novels: "The Solitude of Emperors" and "Ithaca".

question: ‘Alarippu’ is the first dance item of which of the following Indian classical dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Alarippu" (meaning "flowering/blossoming") is the first (invocatory) item in a traditional Bharatanatyam recital. It is a pure dance (nritta) piece through which the dancer warms up and invokes blessings. (अलारिप्पु — भरतनाट्यम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The traditional Bharatanatyam repertoire (Margam) sequence: Alarippu → Jatiswaram → Shabdam → Varnam → Padam → Tillana → Shloka.

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni; famous exponents include Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati and Padma Subrahmanyam.

NOTE

• The eight recognised classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question:
Which of the following are recognised as final goods while estimating the gross domestic product in India?

a. Wheat purchased for making roti in a house

b. Wheat purchased for making roti in a hotel

c. Tea bags used to make tea in a house

d. Tea bags used to make tea in a university hostel canteen
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only a and c.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Final goods are goods purchased for final consumption or investment, not for resale or further production. Only final goods are counted in GDP (to avoid double counting).

◦ (a) Wheat purchased by a household to make roti — consumed at home → final good.

◦ (c) Tea bags used to make tea in a house — consumed at home → final good.

◦ (b) Wheat purchased by a hotel and (d) tea bags used by a canteen are intermediate goods — they are inputs used to produce items that will be sold to customers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Intermediate goods are used up in producing other goods within the year; their value is already included in the value of the final product, so counting them separately would cause double counting.

• GDP (Gross Domestic Product) = money value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country in a year.

NOTE

• The same good can be final or intermediate depending on use: milk bought by a family = final good; milk bought by a sweet shop = intermediate good.

question: The Tunga and Bhadra are tributaries of which river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Krishna.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Tunga and Bhadra rivers rise in the Western Ghats (Karnataka) and merge at Koodli (near Shivamogga) to form the Tungabhadra river, which is the major tributary of the Krishna river. (तुंगभद्रा — कृष्णा की सहायक नदी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Krishna river rises at Mahabaleshwar (Maharashtra) and flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh into the Bay of Bengal.

• Other tributaries of the Krishna: Koyna, Bhima, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Musi and Tungabhadra.

• The Tungabhadra Dam is at Hospet (Karnataka); the ruins of Hampi (Vijayanagara) lie on the banks of the Tungabhadra.

NOTE

• The Krishna is the second largest east-flowing peninsular river after the Godavari (which is called the "Dakshina Ganga").

question: When did India declare itself a Sovereign, Democratic and Republic state with the adoption of the Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 26 January 1950.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India declared itself a Sovereign, Democratic Republic when the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950 — celebrated every year as Republic Day. (26 जनवरी 1950 — गणतंत्र दिवस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day/Samvidhan Divas), and came into effect two months later.

• 26 January was chosen because on this day in 1930 the Indian National Congress had celebrated "Purna Swaraj Day" (following the Lahore Session, December 1929).

• The words "Socialist" and "Secular" were added to the Preamble later by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.

NOTE

• The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to frame the Constitution; Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee and Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the Assembly's President.

question: Diwan-i-Am, containing the marble canopy ornamented with beautiful panels of pietra dura work, is a part of which monument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Red Fort.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Diwan-i-Am (Hall of Public Audience) with its marble canopy ornamented with beautiful pietra dura panels is a part of the Red Fort (Lal Qila), Delhi, built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan (1638–48). (दीवान-ए-आम — लाल किला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Pietra dura" (parchin kari) is the technique of inlaying semi-precious stones into marble to create decorative designs.

• The Red Fort was built when Shah Jahan shifted his capital from Agra to Shahjahanabad (Delhi); it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2007), and the Prime Minister hoists the national flag here every Independence Day.

• Other structures inside the Red Fort: Diwan-i-Khas, Rang Mahal, Mumtaz Mahal, Moti Masjid and Hayat Bakhsh Bagh.

NOTE

• Bibi ka Maqbara (Aurangabad) was built by Aurangzeb's son Azam Shah; Humayun's Tomb (Delhi) was built by Haji Begum; the Taj Mahal (Agra) was built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal.

question: Which of the following is a crop grown in Rabi season in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wheat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wheat" is the most important Rabi crop of India. Rabi crops are sown in winter (October–December) and harvested in summer (April–June). (गेहूँ — रबी फसल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other Rabi crops: barley, gram, peas, mustard, linseed.

• Kharif crops (sown with the onset of monsoon, June–July; harvested September–October): rice, maize, soyabean, jowar, bajra, cotton, groundnut — hence Options 1, 2 and 4 are Kharif crops.

• Zaid crops (short summer season, March–June): watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables.

• Leading wheat-producing states: Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Madhya Pradesh.

NOTE

• Wheat requires cool growing season and bright sunshine at ripening, with 50–75 cm rainfall — conditions typical of north-western India in winter.

question: The 'Secular' word in the Indian Constitution was added to the constitution by __________ Constitutional Amendment Act.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 42nd.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Secular" was added to the Preamble of the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 (during the Emergency, under the Indira Gandhi government). (42वाँ संविधान संशोधन, 1976)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The 42nd Amendment added three words to the Preamble: "Socialist", "Secular" and "Integrity" — the Preamble now reads "Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic".

• The 42nd Amendment is called the "Mini Constitution" because of the large number of changes it made; it also added the Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) and the words for judicial curbs.

• The 44th Amendment (1978) reversed several 42nd-Amendment changes and removed the Right to Property from Fundamental Rights (now a legal right under Article 300A).

NOTE

• Secularism in India means the State has no official religion and treats all religions equally — a part of the basic structure of the Constitution (S. R. Bommai case, 1994).

question: Who among the following Portuguese travellers visited the Vijayanagar empire during the reign of Krishnadevaraya?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Domingo Paes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Domingo Paes, a Portuguese traveller, visited the Vijayanagara Empire during the reign of Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529) of the Tuluva dynasty. He left a glowing account of the city of Vijayanagara (Hampi), calling it "as large as Rome and very beautiful". (डोमिंगो पेस — कृष्णदेवराय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Nicolo de Conti (Italian) visited Vijayanagara during Devaraya I; Abdur Razzaq (Persian) came during Devaraya II; Fernao Nuniz (Portuguese) came during Achyutadevaraya; Athanasius Nikitin (Russian) visited the Bahmani kingdom.

• Krishnadevaraya wrote the Telugu work "Amuktamalyada" and was called "Andhra Bhoja"; his court had the Ashtadiggajas (eight great Telugu poets).

NOTE

• The Vijayanagara Empire (founded 1336 by Harihara and Bukka) had four dynasties: Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu; its capital Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site on the Tungabhadra.

question: Who among the following social reformers established the ‘Prarthana Samaj’ in Bombay in 1876?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atmaram Pandurang.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Prarthana Samaj" was founded in Bombay by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang (in 1867), with the help of Keshab Chandra Sen, as a movement for religious and social reform in Maharashtra. (प्रार्थना समाज — आत्माराम पांडुरंग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Its most famous leader was Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade, who joined it and worked for widow remarriage, women's education, raising the age of marriage and abolition of caste distinctions; R. G. Bhandarkar was another prominent member.

• The Prarthana Samaj was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj of Bengal (founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, 1828) but remained within the Hindu fold, emphasising prayer (prarthana) and social service.

NOTE

• Gopal Hari Deshmukh ("Lokahitawadi") was a Maharashtrian reformer-writer; Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Gopal Ganesh Agarkar founded the newspapers Kesari and Mahratta and the Deccan Education Society.

question: Who among the following founded his Kuchipudi Art Academy at Madras in 1963?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vempati Chinna Satyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary Kuchipudi guru Vempati Chinna Satyam founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy at Madras (Chennai) in 1963. He systematised Kuchipudi technique and spread the dance form across the world. (वेम्पति चिन्ना सत्यम — कुचिपुड़ी कला अकादमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance of Andhra Pradesh, named after the village Kuchipudi (Krishna district); it traditionally combined dance, music and drama, and was performed by male Brahmin troupes.

• Vempati Chinna Satyam received the Padma Bhushan (1998) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award; he trained stars like Vyjayanthimala and Hema Malini.

• Raja and Radha Reddy are a famous Kuchipudi dancer couple.

NOTE

• Siddhendra Yogi is regarded as the founder-father of the Kuchipudi tradition; the dance features the famous Tarangam (dancing on the rim of a brass plate).

question: Which of the following characteristics was used by Aristotle to classify animals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Habitat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Greek philosopher Aristotle classified animals according to their habitat — i.e., whether they lived on land, in water or in the air. This was one of the earliest attempts at biological classification. (अरस्तू — आवास के आधार पर वर्गीकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Aristotle (384–322 BCE) is called the "Father of Biology" and the "Father of Zoology".

• His simple habitat-based grouping was artificial — it put very different animals (e.g., fish and whales) together — so later scientists developed natural systems.

• Carolus Linnaeus ("Father of Taxonomy") gave the binomial nomenclature system and the two-kingdom classification (Plantae and Animalia); R. H. Whittaker (1969) proposed the five-kingdom classification (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia).

NOTE

• Hierarchy of classification: Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species.

question: The 2011 census was the ____________ official survey conducted in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Census of India 2011 was the 15th National Census since the first census of 1872, and the 7th census after Independence. (2011 की जनगणना — 15वीं जनगणना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The first (non-synchronous) census of India was conducted in 1872 under Lord Mayo; the first synchronous (regular) census was in 1881 under Lord Ripon. Since then a census has been held every 10 years.

• The 2011 census motto was "Our Census, Our Future"; the Census Commissioner was C. Chandramouli.

• Key 2011 figures: population 121.09 crore, literacy 74.04% (males 82.14%, females 65.46%), sex ratio 943, density 382 persons/sq km.

• The census is conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs (Census Act, 1948; census is a Union subject — Article 246).

NOTE

• Kerala had the highest literacy (94%) and Bihar the lowest; Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state.

question: As on February 2024, who among the following is the Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarbananda Sonowal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of February 2024, Sarbananda Sonowal was the Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways (and also Minister of AYUSH). He assumed the portfolio in July 2021. (सर्बानंद सोनोवाल — पत्तन, पोत परिवहन और जलमार्ग मंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sarbananda Sonowal was earlier the Chief Minister of Assam (2016–2021).

• At that time, Prahlad Joshi held Parliamentary Affairs, Coal and Mines; Hardeep Singh Puri held Petroleum & Natural Gas and Housing & Urban Affairs; Giriraj Singh held Rural Development and Panchayati Raj.

• Major initiatives of the Ministry: Sagarmala Project (port-led development), Maritime India Vision 2030 and development of National Waterways (NW-1 on the Ganga is the longest).

NOTE

• India has 12 major ports; Mumbai is the largest natural port, and Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT) is the largest container port.

question: If the Glycemic Index (GI) of a specific food is from 70 to 100, then the type of that food is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is High-GI food.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Glycemic Index (GI) ranks carbohydrate foods (on a scale of 0–100) by how quickly they raise blood glucose after eating. A food with GI of 70 to 100 is classified as a High-GI food. (ग्लाइसेमिक इंडेक्स 70–100 — उच्च-जीआई भोजन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• GI classification: Low-GI = 55 or less, Medium-GI = 56–69, High-GI = 70 and above.

• High-GI foods (white bread, white rice, potatoes, sugary items) cause rapid spikes in blood sugar; low-GI foods (whole grains, pulses, most fruits and vegetables) release glucose slowly and are preferred for diabetes management.

• Pure glucose is the reference food with GI = 100.

NOTE

• GI is important for managing diabetes mellitus, a disorder linked to the hormone insulin secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas.

question: In badminton, how high above the ground is the net positioned at the centre?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5 feet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In badminton, the net is 5 feet (1.524 m) high at the centre and 5 feet 1 inch (1.55 m) high at the posts. (बैडमिंटन नेट — केंद्र पर 5 फीट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A badminton court is 44 feet (13.4 m) long and 20 feet (6.1 m) wide for doubles (17 feet wide for singles).

• Badminton is governed globally by the Badminton World Federation (BWF); in India by the Badminton Association of India (BAI).

• Famous Indian shuttlers: Prakash Padukone, Pullela Gopichand (All England champions), Saina Nehwal, P. V. Sindhu (World Champion 2019, Olympic silver 2016 and bronze 2021), Kidambi Srikanth, Lakshya Sen and the doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy–Chirag Shetty.

NOTE

• A badminton match is best of 3 games of 21 points each (rally scoring); a shuttlecock has 16 feathers.

question: In 1905, Hindus and Muslims tied ‘Rakhi’ on each other’s hands to show their unity and their protest against the _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Partition of Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1905, on the day the Partition of Bengal came into effect (16 October 1905), Hindus and Muslims tied rakhis on each other's wrists as a symbol of unity and brotherhood, protesting the British attempt to divide Bengal on communal lines. The Raksha Bandhan protest was inspired by Rabindranath Tagore. (बंगाल विभाजन — 1905, राखी बंधन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Partition of Bengal was announced by Viceroy Lord Curzon (July 1905), ostensibly for administrative convenience but really to "divide and rule".

• It sparked the Swadeshi and Boycott Movement (1905–08); the day was also observed as a day of mourning with fasting and 'Amar Sonar Bangla' being sung.

• The partition was annulled in 1911 by Lord Hardinge II, when the capital was also shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

NOTE

• The Rowlatt Act (1919) led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre; the Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

question:
Which of the following statements are correct postulates of Dalton’s atomic theory?

A. All matter is made up of atoms. These atoms participate in chemical reactions.

B. Atoms might be created or destroyed during a chemical reaction.

C. Atoms of different elements vary in mass and chemical properties.

D. Compounds are combination of atoms in the ratio of whole or fractional numbers.

E. A compound will always have constant relative number and kind of atoms.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, C, E.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to John Dalton's atomic theory (1808):

◦ A is correct — all matter is made of tiny indivisible particles called atoms, which take part in chemical reactions.

◦ C is correct — atoms of different elements differ in mass, size and chemical properties (while atoms of the same element are identical).

◦ E is correct — in a given compound, the relative number and kinds of atoms are always constant (law of definite proportions).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• B is wrong — Dalton stated that atoms can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction (law of conservation of mass), not that they "might be created or destroyed".

• D is wrong — atoms combine in the ratio of small whole numbers, never fractional numbers, to form compounds.

NOTE

• Dalton's theory explained the Law of Conservation of Mass (Lavoisier) and the Law of Constant Proportions (Proust). Later discoveries of electrons (J. J. Thomson), protons and the nucleus (Rutherford) showed that the atom is in fact divisible.

question: The famous Sanskrit grammar book 'Mahabhasya' was written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Patanjali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Sanskrit grammar work "Mahabhasya" ("the Great Commentary") was written by Patanjali (2nd century BCE). It is a detailed commentary on Panini's Ashtadhyayi (and on Katyayana's Varttikas). (महाभाष्य — पतंजलि)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Panini (c. 5th–4th century BCE) wrote the "Ashtadhyayi", the foundational treatise of Sanskrit grammar containing about 4,000 sutras.

• The grammarian Patanjali lived during the time of the Shunga ruler Pushyamitra Shunga and provides valuable historical information about that period.

• A Patanjali is also credited with the "Yoga Sutras", the foundational text of Yoga philosophy.

• Bharat Muni wrote the "Natya Shastra" (treatise on dramaturgy/dance); Ved Vyasa is credited with the Mahabharata and compiling the Vedas.

NOTE

• The three sages of Sanskrit grammar (Muni-traya): Panini (Ashtadhyayi), Katyayana (Varttikas) and Patanjali (Mahabhasya).

question: Hariharan was conferred the Padma Shri in 2004 for his contribution to which of the following fields?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Art - Music.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Hariharan, the renowned playback and ghazal singer, was conferred the Padma Shri in 2004 for his contribution to the field of Art – Music. (हरिहरन — पद्म श्री 2004, कला-संगीत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Hariharan is famous for songs like "Tu Hi Re" (Bombay), "Chanda Re" and the album "Colonial Cousins" (with Lesle Lewis); he has won National Film Awards for playback singing.

• The Padma Awards — Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri — are announced every year on Republic Day eve and conferred by the President of India; they were instituted in 1954.

• Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India (after Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan).

NOTE

• Padma awards are given in fields such as art, literature and education, sports, medicine, social work, science and engineering, public affairs, civil service, and trade and industry.
